{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Subject:** Playbook review findings — MSA as received from Vendor

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The core risk-allocation architecture is unusually strong for us: limitation of liability (§21), assignment and change of control (§24), licence grant (§13), warranties (§19), Vendor insurance (§18), audit rights (§22) and the auto-renewal/uplift mechanic (§8) all meet our preferred positions and require no redline.

The problems are concentrated in three places:

1. **A cluster of Customer-side restraints that sit in walk-away territory** — the three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights" (§2.1), the disclose-and-match obligation before engaging another provider (§7.2), a 24-month all-territory non-compete and a one-way 24-month no-hire (both numbered §12.4). Each of these directly contradicts §12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We read the internal inconsistency as a drafting artefact and propose to delete the restraints and let §12.3 govern.
2. **Three missing protections.** There is **no indemnification article at all** — the outline jumps from §19 to §21, while §9.3, §19.4, §21.3 and §30.5 all cross-refer to indemnities that do not exist (§9.3 points to "Section 20.5", a broken reference). There is **no termination for convenience** anywhere in §9, against a three-year term and a take-or-pay commitment. And there is **no post-termination transition assistance or data-return obligation**: §16.5 carves Customer Data out of the return/destroy duty and defers to "Sections 11 and 15", but Section 11 does not exist in the document.
3. **Two drafting conflicts to resolve.** §14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created for us, with only a revocable, term-limited licence back; and §28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts, which conflicts with §28.2 (exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County).

Of 19 findings, 12 are compliant and require no action. Seven require redlines, of which eight items (including the two rules breached by §7.2) engage our walk-away positions.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | §21.1 (with §§21.2–21.4, §18.2) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; full Excluded Claims set. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment / change of control | Compliant | §24.1 (with §§24.2–24.4, §13.3) | Free Customer assignment on notice; Vendor restricted; no repricing or acceleration on our change of control. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties on Customer | Compliant | §27.3 | No Customer-payable LDs, penalties or early-termination fees. Take-or-pay in §2.1 addressed under MINCOMMIT. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | §13.1 (with §§13.2–13.3) | Affiliates, contractors and Authorized Users covered; paid-up perpetual rights to Vendor Technology. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Vendor audit rights | Compliant | §22.1 (with §§22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, no system or unrelated-data access. |
| Medium | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | §14.2 | Vendor owns every Deliverable; our licence is revocable and term-limited. Fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable licence). Redline flips ownership with assignment on creation, preserving Vendor Technology under §14.3. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | §8.2 (with §8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day reminder with deadline extension; uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | §19.1 (with §§19.2–19.5, §6.2) | Exceeds preferred: hosted-service conformity for the whole subscription term; disclaimer is mutual and carved back. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 | De facto exclusivity/ROFR for the full term, no category limit, no 12-month cap, no performance exit. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | §28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts; outside the accepted list and conflicts with §28.2. Redline selects New York law and New York County courts. |
| Low | INDEMN — Vendor indemnification | **Missing** | No indemnity article (cross-refs at §9.3, §19.4, §21.3, §30.5) | No Vendor IP indemnity at all; §9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" is broken. Insert Section 20. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | §18.1 (with §18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber and privacy 5M, term plus one year; insurance does not cap liability. |
| Low | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | **Deviation** | §7.2 | Open-ended obligation to disclose and match any better third-party offer; unlimited as to product, term and comparison method. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitment | **Deviation** | §2.1 | Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; no convenience exit in §9. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 (duplicate-numbered, p0046) | 24 months post-term, any competing product or service, any territory, no internal-development or acquisition carve-out. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | §12.4 | One-way 24-month outright no-hire covering every Vendor employee, expressly negating the general-advertising carve-out. Conflicts with §12.3. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | §9 (only §§9.1–9.3, all cause-based) | No convenience right against a three-year term; §2.1 strips reduction and termination rights. Insert §9.4. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | §10.2 (with §16.5) | No transition-assistance obligation and no data return, export or certified deletion; §16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. Insert §10.3. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following engage our walk-away positions and, on the current drafting, we cannot sign:

1. **§2.1 — three-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights.** Multi-year take-or-pay with no exit. Fallback offered: commitment confined to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, settled by true-up rather than penalty. Preferred redline: delete, with Fees payable only for Services ordered or used.
2. **No termination for convenience (§9).** Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term. Redline inserts §9.4 — termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no Vendor convenience right during a committed term, plus a conforming edit to §2.1.
3. **No Vendor indemnity.** No IP infringement defence or indemnity anywhere, and §9.3's remedy cross-reference is broken. Redline inserts a single Section 20 (IP, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breach, gross negligence and wilful misconduct), with notice/control/cooperation procedure, procure-modify-replace-refund remedies at 20.5, and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our own breach of law.
4. **§7.2 — disclose-and-match before engaging another provider.** Breaches both EXCLUSIVITY and MFN independently: an open-ended right of first refusal restraining our sourcing freedom for the full term, and an unlimited Customer-side MFN. Redline negates the obligation.
5. **§12.4 — 24-month, all-territory non-compete.** Post-term restraint beyond 12 months with effectively undefined scope. Redline deletes, leaving §12.3 to govern; fallback offered of a term-only restriction on a single named product.
6. **§12.4 — one-way 24-month no-hire.** Outright hiring ban on all Vendor employees with no advertising or unsolicited-application carve-out. Redline deletes; fallback offered of a narrow mutual 12-month non-solicit.
7. **§28.1 — Singapore law and exclusive Singapore courts.** Exclusive foreign venue outside the accepted list, and inconsistent with §28.2. Redline changes only the governing-law and forum words to New York law and the New York County courts; §28.3 escalation is unchanged.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven walk-away items above plus §14.2 (deliverable ownership flipped to Customer with assignment on creation, Vendor retaining Vendor Technology under §14.3) and new §10.3 (up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, certified deletion thereafter, subject to routine backup and legal retention consistent with §16.5).
2. **Raise the §12.3 inconsistency directly with Vendor.** §2.1, §7.2 and both §12.4 clauses each contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement in §12.3 that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume or no-hire commitment. We should ask Vendor to confirm the restraints were included in error; that framing should carry most of this cluster without negotiation.
3. **Flag the structural defects for clean-up in the same pass:** the missing Section 20 and the broken §9.3 cross-reference to "Section 20.5"; the reference in §16.5 to a non-existent Section 11; Section 23 containing no operative text; and the duplicate clause numbering at §7.2 and §12.4.
4. **Confirm the commercial position on minimum commitment and term** with the business owner before we send, so we know whether to open at deletion of §2.1 or at the 12-month reducible fallback.
5. **Confirm the service-level exhibit** referenced at §2.2. The body contains no service-credit regime; §9.3's repeated-critical-miss termination right depends on the exhibit's definitions, which we have not reviewed.

No action is required on the twelve compliant findings; several (notably §§8, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 24) run materially in our favour and should be protected from erosion in any Vendor counter-draft."}
